title: Stress binds distributed modules into one larger homeostatic loop

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Stress binds distributed modules into one larger homeostatic loop

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Stress, defined as a system-level response to the difference between current state and a setpoint, scales Selves by binding modules that sense and act at different scales and locations into one global homeostatic loop; propagated stress signals recruit distant sub-agents to act so as to reduce their own stress.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: A Proposal for a Framework › Specific Conceptual Components of the Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere Framework

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Stress is a systemic response to a difference between current state and a desired setpoint; it is an essential component to scaling of Selves because it enables different modules (which sense and act on things at different scales and in distributed locations) to be bound together in one global homeostatic loop (toward a larger purpose).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds”, Frontiers in systems neuroscience (2022), doi:10.3389/fnsys.2022.768201; section “Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: A Proposal for a Framework › Specific Conceptual Components of the Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere Framework”. Scope: Multicellular organisms and other multi-scale agents

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-tame-09: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.45

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Signal propagation and coordinated homeostasis are measurable for particular tissues. Existing datasets can test pieces of the mechanism but not the broader assertion that stress creates a larger Self.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure a propagated stress signal, local setpoint deviations, and compensatory actions across modules; test whether blocking propagation reduces coordinated return to a global setpoint beyond local-control predictions.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Stress and Self-scaling have multiple operational meanings.

Relevant perturbation-plus-readout datasets are sparse.

Observational expression data do not isolate global-loop causality.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.28
operationalizability: 0.58
analysis feasibility: 0.55
data existence: 0.45
discriminating power: 0.42

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Long-range injury signals and compensatory responses are reported in a handful of regeneration papers, as summaries rather than a shared dataset. Those records can show that a wound changes distant tissue. They do not contain the joint measurement of setpoint error, recruitment, and error reduction that would separate one homeostatic loop from ordinary coupling.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Impose a local deviation from a measured setpoint, record whether distant modules change their activity, and block the candidate signal; binding holds if remote action reduces the original error and fails when the signal is blocked.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Setpoint error, remote recruitment, and error reduction are rarely measured together outside a few injury preparations.

Published injury-spread results cover a small slice of multicellular organisms.

Ordinary physiological coupling spreads signals without binding modules into one homeostatic individual.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.3
analysis feasibility: 0.4
data existence: 0.4
operationalizability: 0.5
discriminating power: 0.4
